mutig.et: From Middle High German muotic, from Old High German muotag, from Proto-Germanic *mōdagaz; equivalent to Mut + -ig.

s: Er sagt, er glaubt nicht, dass ich eine Mutantin bin, aber manche Mutanten erkennt man schwer.
A boy (especially a choirboy) whose voice is breaking due to puberty.
Ich habe kein Zuhause mehr, ich habe meine Mutter verloren, meine Stimme dazu. Ich bin ein Mutant.
I don't have a home anymore, I lost my mother, my voice too. I am a mutant.

Dann änderte sich alles. „Man spürt, wie die Stimme anders wird, wie sie beim Singen einbricht“, sagt Simon. Er traf auf einmal nicht mehr sicher alle Töne. […] Simon wurde mit 14 Jahren zum „Mutant“.
Then everything changed. "You can feel how your voice is changing, how it breaks when you're singing," said Simon. He suddenly couldn't hit all the notes […] Simon became a "mutant" at 14 years old.
alternative form for the dative singular of Mut

Mutter.et: From Middle High German muoter, from Old High German muoter, from Proto-West Germanic *mōder, from Proto-Germanic *mōdēr, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr. Compare Dutch moeder, English mother, Danish moder, Swedish moder.

From Middle High German muoter, from Old High German muoter, from Proto-West Germanic *mōder, from Proto-Germanic *mōdēr, from Proto-Indo-European *méh₂tēr. Compare Dutch moeder, English mother, Danish moder, Swedish moder.
Originally the same as etymology 1, but secondarily distinguished in the plural; so denoted by a sexual metaphor, which is also found in other languages. Compare for example Dutch moer.

s: Ich wünschte, ich hätte den Mut, auf einer Bühne vor Publikum zu sprechen.
I wish I had the courage to speak on stage before an audience.
Mut.et: From Middle High German muot, from Old High German muot, from Proto-West Germanic *mōd, from Proto-Germanic *mōdaz. Cognate with Dutch moed, English mood.

s: bonnet, reticulum, the second compartment of the stomach of a ruminant
Mütze.et: From Middle High German almuʒ, ultimately from Medieval Latin almutia (“hood, cowl”), of unknown origin. Compare Latin amictus (“clothed, veiled”).

s: to desire, to demand, to set one's mind on something
to apply for a mining concession
muten.et: From Middle High German muoten, from Old High German muoten, muotôn.

s: Ich hab ihn gemutet, aber der Rotz kommt durch.
I muted him, but the crap gets through.
Klicken Sie auf die Section, die Sie muten möchten.
Click on the section that you would like to mute.
the language one has learnt from one’s mother (chiefly in the case of two parents with different languages)
Türkisch ist meine Muttersprache und Deutsch meine Vatersprache.
Turkish is my mother’s language and German is my father’s language.
ancestor language, parent language (language from which another is derived)
Latein ist die Muttersprache des Romanischen.
Latin is the ancestor of Romance.
Muttersprache.et: Loan translation and/or phonetic adaptation of Middle Low German môdersprâke, itself possibly a loan translation of Latin lingua materna. Analyzable as Mutter (“mother”) + Sprache (“language”).

s: Es bleibt daher nichts anderes übrig, als zu mutmaßen.
So there's nothing to be done except speculating.
to speculate, to assume, to suspect (an explanation or claim)
Er mutmaßt, dass es so gewesen ist.
He is speculating that that was the case.

s: native speaker (male or of unspecified gender) (a person who grew up with a particular language as their mother tongue)
"Es ist zu befürchten, dass das famose Muttersöhnchen [Erich] Kästner das ernsthaft für einen legitimen Grund hält, in Deutschland zu bleiben", schreibt [Florian] Illies.
Muttersöhnchen.et: Compound of Mutter (“mother”) + Söhnchen (“diminutive of Sohn (little son)”).

s: Da stand ich nun unter Gottes freiem Himmel wieder auf dem stillen Platze mutterseelen allein, wie ich gestern angekommen war.
There I stood now under God's open sky, again in the silent square, forsaken and forlorn, just as when I had arrived the day before.
Schnee und Regen fällt und große braune Wasserlachen wachsen an. Niemand ist da; nur sie; mutterseelenallein.
Snow and rain falls and big brown puddles grow. No one is there; only she; utterly alone.
mutterseelenallein.et: 18th century, from earlier mutterallein (16th c., literally “mother-alone”), which is either “as alone as a child in the womb” or more likely “as alone as a child bereft of its mother”. The contemporary form is equivalent to Mutterseele + -n- + allein, wherein…

s: maternally, from the mother's side, on the mother's side

Mutex.et: Borrowed from English mutex, short for mutually exclusive.

a ewe (female sheep) that has a lamb
motherland: mainland as opposed to a colony
Kolonialdialekte sind in der Regel einheitlicher als die Dialekte des Mutterlandes.
Colonial dialects are usually more uniform than the dialects of the motherland.
motherland: country where something originated, where someone’s ancestors came from
England gilt als Mutterland des Fußballs.
England is considered the motherland of (association) football.

Mutterkorn.et: Mutter + Korn, associated in folk etymology with Gebärmutter, from its therapeutic use in gynecology.

s: Mutterisch wird als kindliche Sprache verstanden, die – stark überbetont – Vorgänge wiederholend beschreibt. Überhaupt ist Sprache eine zentrale Erkenntnisquelle für Kinder.
Die Mutprobe bestand darin, sich so weit wie möglich auf die Eisfläche hinauszuwagen.
The dare consisted of venturing out onto the surface of the ice as far as possible.
